title: Kavi methods references from Arnav123-s public starred repositories
purpose: These repositories are design and evaluation references. They are not a training corpus, and no source code or documentation is ingested automatically.

repositories.study_role: low-bit and resource-aware model design comparator
repositories.kavi_question: Can compact persistent state preserve useful behavior under a measured resource ceiling?

repositories.study_role: agent architecture and bounded orchestration reference
repositories.kavi_question: Which parts should remain external evaluators rather than model-controlled behavior?

repositories.study_role: message contracts and distributed-system organization reference
repositories.kavi_question: How can Kavi make pathway messages and state transitions inspectable?
How should Kavi choose the next falsifiable architecture experiment?
Which parts are unsuitable for a small local core and should remain excluded?
How should data, training, caching, and evaluation remain separate?
How can claims be rejected when evidence is weak or unstable?
When does a physical analogy produce a testable algorithm instead of only a metaphor?
Which constraint mechanisms are fair baselines for Kavi's local update rules?
What changes, if any, distinguish this fork from its upstream method?
Can retrieval remain external and measured rather than be misreported as internal model memory?
How can parsing and executable meaning be tested before broad language claims?
Which generated, checkable tasks provide a fair early core benchmark?

review_rule: Inspect an exact commit, license, and relevant files before copying, running, or deriving training material from any repository.
